mainTopic: Early פדיון הבן, whose redemption comes first (father or son), and the מנה צורי coin standard
overview: This עמוד finishes the מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about a father who redeems his בכור before day thirty, after the כהן has already used up the coins. רב compares it to קידושין that take effect later. שמואל answers that a man can betroth a woman right now, but a father cannot redeem his son before day thirty, and the הלכה follows שמואל. Two challenges from the משנה are answered by saying the משנה means a case where the coins still exist on day thirty. Next, the גמרא discusses a man who must redeem both himself and his son: the רבנן put the father first, and רבי יהודה puts the son first. רבי ירמיה explains that with only five סלעים everyone agrees the father comes first. They argue only when there is both sold and free land, which depends on whether a תורה debt is like a loan written in a שטר. Finally, a new משנה teaches that פדיון הבן and other fixed תורה payments use the שקל הקודש by the מנה צורי, and three אמוראים explain what that coin standard is.

steps.title: רב finishes his comparison to קידושין
steps.stepSummary: רב concludes that early פדיון works, just like early קידושין works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes רב's argument. Just as קידושין set for 'after thirty days' take effect even if the money was used up, early פדיון also works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right before this, רב pointed to the case of a man who says 'be betrothed to me after thirty days.' There the קידושין take effect even if the money is gone by then. רב says פדיון הבן is the same, so the son is redeemed.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new idea. It is the last line of רב's comparison to קידושין, which started on the previous עמוד.

phrases.english: Here too, it is no different.
phrases.notes: The conclusion of רב's comparison to קידושין after thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב's comparison from the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that the son is redeemed even if the coins were used up before day thirty.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of קידושין that take effect after thirty days, which work even if the money was used up.

steps.title: שמואל shows why קידושין is different
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the comparison fails: the man could betroth her now, but a father cannot redeem his son now.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל can say to you: There, it is in his power to betroth her right now. Here, it is not in his power to redeem him right now.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל pushes back on רב's comparison to קידושין and points out a key difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man could marry the woman today if he wanted, so his money can work even when the קידושין are delayed. A father cannot redeem his son before day thirty at all. So once the money is gone, nothing is left to make the פדיון happen when the time comes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general rule: an action can work 'later' only if the person could have done it now.

phrases.english: And Shmuel can say to you:
There — it is in his power to betroth her from now,
here — it is not in his power to redeem him from now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב's comparison from Step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between delayed קידושין and early פדיון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two cases differ: קידושין could be done right away, but פדיון cannot happen before day thirty.

steps.title: The halacha follows שמואל here
steps.stepSummary: Usually we follow רב in ritual matters, but here the הלכה is like שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though we hold that wherever רב and שמואל disagree, the הלכה follows רב in ritual matters and שמואל in money matters, here the הלכה follows שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling: the הלכה is like שמואל, so a son redeemed early, where the money is gone, is not redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule is to follow רב in ritual matters (איסורי) and שמואל in money matters (דיני). Here the גמרא makes an exception and rules like שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold as an established rule

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows שמואל: if a father redeems his son before day thirty and the money is no longer around, the son is not redeemed.

phrases.english: And even though we maintain,
that wherever Rav and Shmuel disagree —
the halakha follows Rav in ritual matters
and follows Shmuel in monetary matters,
here the halakha follows Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling on the מחלוקת after שמואל's answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows שמואל, as an exception to the usual rule for disagreements between רב and שמואל.

steps.title: Challenge to שמואל from the משנה about a baby who died
steps.stepSummary: The משנה suggests that if the baby had lived, the early payment would have worked, which goes against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: If the baby dies within thirty days, even though the father gave the money to the כהן, the כהן must return the five סלעים. The reason is that the baby died. This implies that if he did not die, his son is redeemed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that seems to show early פדיון works, which contradicts שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the money is returned only because the baby died. That suggests that if the baby had lived, the payment made before day thirty would count as a valid פדיון. That is רב's view, not שמואל's.

keyTerms.meaning: Sela coins (the redemption price is five)

phrases.english: We learned: If he died within thirty days,
even though he gave the money to the priest —
the priest must return the five sela to him.
The reason is that he died,
but if he did not die — his son is redeemed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's position, which was just accepted as the הלכה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that early פדיון does not work.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading the משנה in reverse: since the money is returned only because the baby died, a living baby would be redeemed by the early payment.

steps.title: The משנה is about money still with the כהן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a case where the coins still exist on day thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where the money still exists.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by limiting the משנה to a case where the כהן still has the coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the coins are still with the כהן when day thirty arrives, the פדיון can take effect at that moment. שמואל agrees with that case. His disagreement with רב is only about a case where the money was already used up.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?
Where the money still exists.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that early payment always works if the baby lives.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only means the case where the money is still with the כהן on day thirty, which שמואל agrees with.

steps.title: Second challenge from the משנה about the father's death
steps.stepSummary: The משנה implies that if people say the son was redeemed, he is redeemed, even though any such פדיון happened before day thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The son is assumed not to have been redeemed until people tell him that he was redeemed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another line of the משנה to challenge שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is about a father who died within thirty days, so any פדיון he did must have happened early. Yet the משנה says that if people report he redeemed the son, it counts. That suggests early פדיון works, against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a source is being brought)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
He is presumed not to have been redeemed
until they tell him that he was redeemed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against שמואל from the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that early פדיון does not work.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The father died before day thirty, so any פדיון he did was early. Yet the משנה accepts it once people report it.

steps.title: Same answer: the coins still exist
steps.stepSummary: This משנה is also about a case where the coins are still with the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is a case where the money still exists, intact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge the same way as the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the coins are still with the כהן on day thirty, the פדיון takes effect then, and שמואל agrees. So neither line of the משנה goes against שמואל.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל agrees that early פדיון works if the coins still exist on day thirty. He only disagrees when the money was already used up.

phrases.english: There too
it is where the money still exists, intact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6 using the same answer as Step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to accept a פדיון done before day thirty in any situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only means the case where the money is still with the כהן on day thirty.

steps.title: A תנא recites a ברייתא saying early redemption works
steps.stepSummary: A תנא reads a ברייתא in front of רב יהודה: if someone redeems his son before day thirty, the son is redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught in front of רב יהודה: Someone who redeems his son within thirty days, his son is redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: A reciter of ברייתות reads a teaching saying that a פדיון done before day thirty still counts. This sets up רב יהודה's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא matches רב's view and goes against שמואל's view. A ברייתא is normally a strong source, so its wording seems to give רב support.

keyTerms.meaning: A professional reciter of ברייתות in the בית מדרש
Within thirty days, before the obligation to redeem begins

phrases.english: A tanna taught in front of Rav Yehuda:

phrases.aramaic: הַפּוֹדֶה אֶת בְּנוֹ בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
phrases.english: One who redeems his son within thirty days,
his son is redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenges from the משנה were answered, a ברייתא is brought that openly states the opposite of שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this ברייתא, a פדיון done before day thirty is valid.

steps.title: רב יהודה objects because שמואל said otherwise
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה tells the תנא that שמואל ruled the son is not redeemed, so how can the תנא say he is?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: שמואל said his son is not redeemed, and you say his son is redeemed?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה, a student of שמואל, pushes back against the ברייתא as it was recited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה does not accept this version of the ברייתא, because his teacher שמואל ruled that a פדיון before day thirty does not work. His point is that the ברייתא should not be recited or followed this way.

keyTerms.meaning: And you say?! (an expression of surprise or objection)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר אֵין בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי,
phrases.english: He said to him: Shmuel said his son is not redeemed,
and you say his son is redeemed?!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר אֵין בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי, וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds directly to the ברייתא recited in step 8 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that an early פדיון is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling contradicts שמואל's clear ruling, which רב יהודה treats as authoritative.

steps.title: The halacha follows שמואל here, even though this is a ritual matter
steps.stepSummary: Normally the הלכה follows רב in ritual laws and שמואל in monetary laws, but here the הלכה follows שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though we hold like רב in ritual laws and like שמואל in monetary laws, here the הלכה is like שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling: a פדיון before day thirty does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether a son is redeemed is a ritual question (איסורא), so normally we would follow רב. The גמרא makes a specific exception and rules like שמואל, which fits רב יהודה's objection.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual laws (what is permitted or forbidden)

steps.whatToRemember: A פדיון done before day thirty does not work. This is an exception to the usual rule that we follow רב in ritual matters.

phrases.english: And even though we hold
like Rav in ritual laws and like Shmuel in monetary laws,
here the halacha is like Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקַיְימָא לַן כְּרַב בְּאִיסּוּרֵי וְכִשְׁמוּאֵל בְּדִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the dispute in favor of שמואל, in line with רב יהודה's objection.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows שמואל: a son redeemed before day thirty is not redeemed.

steps.title: New topic: the father's own redemption comes before his son's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and then a ברייתא: if a father needs to redeem both himself and his son, his own פדיון comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If he needs to be redeemed and his son needs to be redeemed, he comes before his son, etc. The רבנן taught in a ברייתא: If he needs to be redeemed and his son needs to be redeemed, he comes before his son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting the משנה. It then brings a ברייתא with the same ruling, which sets up the dispute in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a בכור whose own father never redeemed him, and who now has a בכור son of his own. The ברייתא is quoted because it also contains רבי יהודה's dissenting view.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs redeeming and his son needs redeeming

phrases.english: [The Mishnah:] He is to be redeemed and his son is to be redeemed,
he comes before his son, etc.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הוּא לִפְדּוֹת וּבְנוֹ לִפְדּוֹת
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: He is to be redeemed and his son is to be redeemed,
he comes before his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא לִפְדּוֹת וּבְנוֹ לִפְדּוֹת הוּא קוֹדֵם לִבְנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, the father's own פדיון comes before his son's.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says the son comes first
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees: the son's פדיון comes first, because the father's own פדיון was his father's מצוה, while his son's פדיון is his own מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: His son comes first, because the מצוה of redeeming him was on his own father, while the מצוה of redeeming his son is on him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues and gives a reason why the son should be redeemed first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה placed the מצוה of redeeming a בכור on the father. Since the grandfather failed to do it, it is not really this man's own original מצוה, while redeeming his son is. So he should first do the מצוה that is his.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה to redeem him is on his father

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: His son comes before him,
since the מצוה [of redeeming] him is on his father,
and the מצוה of [redeeming] his son is on him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the son's פדיון comes first, because it is the father's own מצוה.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: with only five סלעים, everyone agrees the father comes first
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה narrows the dispute. If there are only five סלעים, enough for one פדיון, everyone agrees the father redeems himself first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Everyone agrees that where there are only five סלעים, he comes before his son.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה limits the argument by naming a case where even רבי יהודה agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first we might think רבי יהודה always puts the son first. רבי ירמיה says that when there is only enough money for one פדיון, even רבי יהודה agrees the father redeems himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Five סלעים, the amount for one פדיון הבן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה always says the son comes first. According to רבי ירמיה, when there is only enough money for one פדיון, רבי יהודה agrees the father comes first.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: Everyone agrees
where there are only five sela'im,
he comes before his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With only five סלעים, all opinions agree the father redeems himself first.

steps.title: The reason: a person's own מצוה takes priority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why everyone agrees, and answers that a מצוה on one's own body is more important.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because his own מצוה is more important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי ירמיה's statement and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being redeemed yourself is a מצוה that concerns your own body, which is more important than a מצוה done for someone else. This reason is strong enough to outweigh רבי יהודה's argument when only one פדיון is possible.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because his own מצוה is preferable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי ירמיה's point of agreement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does everyone agree the father comes first when there are only five סלעים?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מצוה that concerns one's own person takes priority.

steps.title: The real dispute: sold land and free land
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the argument is about a father who has land worth five סלעים that he sold (משועבדים) and land worth five סלעים that he still owns (בני חורין).
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue is a case where there are five [סלעים' worth of] liened property and five [סלעים' worth of] free property.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה defines the exact case of the dispute. This sets up the explanation in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משועבדים is land the father sold after a debt was already on him, so a creditor with the right kind of debt can take it from the buyer. בני חורין is land the father still owns, which can pay any debt. The question is whether the כהן can collect a פדיון from the sold land.

keyTerms.meaning: Liened property that was sold to others but is still tied to an earlier debt
Free property, still owned by the debtor

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא חָמֵשׁ מְשׁוּעְבָּדוֹת
phrases.english: Where they argue is where there are five [sela'im of] liened property
and five [sela'im of] free property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After naming where everyone agrees, רבי ירמיה names where they argue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute applies only when there is both sold and free property, each worth five סלעים.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's principle: a תורה debt is like a written loan
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that a debt written in the תורה, such as פדיון, works like a loan written in a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds: A loan written in the תורה is like one written in a document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the principle behind רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan backed by a שטר can be collected even from land the borrower later sold. רבי יהודה says a debt created by the תורה has the same power, so a פדיון obligation can be collected from sold land. The רבנן disagree, as step 18 explains, so for them only free land can be used.

keyTerms.meaning: A debt written in the תורה (a financial obligation set by the תורה)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: מִלְוָה הַכְּתוּבָה בַּתּוֹרָה —
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds: A loan written in the Torah
is like one written in a document,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: מִלְוָה הַכְּתוּבָה בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the legal principle behind רבי יהודה's view in the case from step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a debt set by the תורה can be collected from sold land, just like a loan with a שטר.

steps.title: Both redemptions get done: the father's from sold land, the son's from free land
steps.stepSummary: The כהן collects the father's own פדיון from the sold land, and the father uses the free land to redeem his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for his own [פדיון], the כהן goes and collects from the sold property, and with these five [סלעים of] free property he redeems his son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies רבי יהודה's principle to the case and shows that both people get redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's own debt began when he was born, before he sold the land, so it can be collected from that land. The son's debt began only after the sale, so it can only be paid from free land. That is why רבי יהודה uses the free land for the son and lets the כהן collect the father's פדיון from the buyers.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says the father comes first. רבי יהודה says the son comes first. רבי ירמיה explains that they argue only when there is both sold and free land. רבי יהודה treats a תורה debt like a שטר, so the father's own פדיון is collected from the sold land and the free land redeems the son.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a broader idea: whether a debt created by the תורה has the collection power of a written loan. That question comes up in many other areas of monetary law.

phrases.english: And for his own [redemption, the kohen] goes and collects from the liened property,
and with these five [sela'im of] free property
he redeems his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle from step 16 to the case defined in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי יהודה, the free land redeems the son and the כהן collects the father's own פדיון from the sold land, so both מצוות are fulfilled.

steps.title: The רבנן's reasoning: a תורה debt is not like a written loan
steps.stepSummary: רבנן hold that a debt written in the תורה does not work like a loan written in a שטר. So the כהן cannot collect from the sold land, and the father's own מצוה comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן hold: a loan written in the תורה is not like one written in a document. Therefore his own מצוה comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the other side of the argument, the view of רבנן. This finishes the explanation that began with רבי יהודה's view in steps 16-17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the father's own פדיון is like a loan written in a שטר, so it can be collected from the sold land, and the free land is left for the son. רבנן say a תורה debt has no such lien, so buyers had no warning and the sold land cannot be taken. That leaves only the free five סלעים, and the father uses them for himself, because a מצוה on his own body comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: A debt that comes from the תורה itself, not from a written contract
As if it were written in a loan document, which creates a lien on the debtor's land

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה says a תורה debt equals a written loan, so the father pays for himself from sold land and redeems his son with the free land. רבנן say it is not like a written loan, so the father redeems himself with the free land, because his own מצוה comes first.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole dispute turns on one general question: does a debt created by the תורה give the creditor a lien on land the debtor has sold? This question comes up in many other places in ש״ס.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
a loan that is written in the Torah
is not like one written in a document,
phrases.notes: Buyers had no warning, so the sold land cannot be taken.

phrases.english: therefore his own מצוה is preferable.
phrases.notes: He redeems himself with the free land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה's reasoning from steps 16-17, which closes רבי ירמיה's explanation of the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תורה debt creates no lien like a written loan, so the father's own מצוה takes priority over his son's פדיון.

steps.title: New משנה: the five סלעים of a בכור are measured by the מנה צורי
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that the five סלעים of פדיון הבן are measured with the מנה צורי, the high-value coin standard of Tyre.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The five סלעים of a son are paid according to the מנה צורי.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us which coin standard is used to measure the five סלעים of פדיון הבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coins in different places held different amounts of silver. The משנה rules that the 'שקל הקודש' the תורה mentions follows the heavier, purer Tyrian standard, not the cheaper local coins.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
A silver coin, the same as the biblical שקל
The Tyrian מנה, a high-quality silver coin standard from the city of Tyre

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The five selaim of the firstborn son
are by the Tyrian maneh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the measure of the money payment rather than the order of priority.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פדיון הבן is paid in the Tyrian coin standard.

steps.title: Other fixed תורה payments also use the שקל הקודש
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists more fixed amounts from the תורה: 30 for a slave killed by an ox, 50 for אונס and מפתה, and 100 for מוציא שם רע. All of them are paid in the שקל הקודש, using the מנה צורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Thirty for an עבד, fifty for an אונס and a מפתה, and a hundred for a מוציא שם רע: all are in the שקל הקודש, by the מנה צורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה extends the same rule to other fixed payments in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some of these פסוקים do not say 'שקל הקודש' at all. The משנה still teaches that every fixed תורה amount uses the same high Sanctuary standard.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who forces a young unmarried girl; he pays fifty
A man who seduces a young unmarried girl; he pays fifty
A husband who falsely claims his bride was not a בתולה; he pays one hundred
The Sanctuary shekel, the official תורה standard

phrases.english: Thirty of a slave,
phrases.notes: Paid when an ox kills an עבד כנעני

phrases.english: fifty of a rapist and of a seducer,
and one hundred of one who defames
all of them are in the Sanctuary shekel,
by the Tyrian maneh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the coin standard from step 19 to other fixed תורה payments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All fixed תורה payments are measured in the שקל הקודש, using the Tyrian standard.

steps.title: All may be paid with money or goods, except the מחצית השקל
steps.stepSummary: Every one of these payments may be made with coins or with goods worth that amount. The only exception is the yearly half-שקל given to the מקדש, which must be given as coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them may be paid with money or with things worth money, except for the שקלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes by explaining how these payments may be made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'נפדין' here simply means 'paid.' Goods of equal value are acceptable for all these payments. Only the annual מחצית השקל must be actual coins.

keyTerms.meaning: Something worth money, such as goods or movable items
Here: the yearly half-shekel donated to the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: 'חוץ משקלים' does NOT refer to the payments just listed. It means the yearly מחצית השקל, which must be given in coins.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rules: everything is measured by the Tyrian standard, and everything may be paid with goods worth money, except the yearly half-שקל.

phrases.english: And all of them are paid
with money or with the equivalent of money,
except for the shekalim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the method of payment after the measure was given in steps 19-20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money or goods are acceptable for all these payments except the half-שקל, which must be coins.

steps.title: What is a מנה צורי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'מנה צורי' in order to define them.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'A מנה צורי.' What does that mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a phrase from the משנה. This sets up the explanations of the אמוראים that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not written out in words. Quoting the phrase alone works as a request to define it. The answers that follow tell us what it means in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: A Tyrian maneh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the key term from the משנה in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The real meaning and practical value of 'מנה צורי'.

steps.title: רבי אסי: the מנה used in צור
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי explains that it means the מנה coinage used in the city of צור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: the מנה of צור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי gives the first explanation: it is simply the money standard of צור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer identifies where the coin comes from. It does not convert the amount into a coin people use today.

keyTerms.meaning: Tyre, a city known for high-quality silver coins

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:
the maneh of Tyre.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It means the coinage used in Tyre.

steps.title: רבי אמי: an Arabian דינר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says the five סלעים are equal to an Arabian gold דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: an Arabian דינר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי gives a second explanation, using a coin that people knew in his time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of naming the place the coin comes from, רבי אמי gives a practical equal value: the full פדיון equals one Arabian gold דינר. The text has a correction in brackets: the reading ערבא was changed to ערביא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
an Arabian dinar.
phrases.notes: The text corrects ערבא to ערביא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The five סלעים equal one Arabian gold דינר.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: five Syrian coins, eight to a דינר
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says there is a Syrian coin, eight of which are sold for a gold דינר. One gives five of those for פדיון הבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: a Syrian איסתרא, eight of which are sold for a דינר; five of them are for פדיון הבן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives a third explanation, in terms of a common Syrian coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא gives an exact amount: the father pays five Syrian coins, where eight of them buy one large gold דינר. This turns the משנה's 'מנה צורי' into a coin people actually used.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeeming a firstborn son from a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: Three אמוראים define the 'מנה צורי': the Tyrian coinage (רבי אסי), an Arabian gold דינר (רבי אמי), and five Syrian coins, eight of which equal a gold דינר (רבי חנינא).

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina says:
a Syrian istera,
eight of which are sold for a dinar,
five of them are for the redemption of the son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Five Syrian coins, eight of which equal a gold דינר.
